sources.title: Keren L, Klein A, Bar-Shachar Y, Liakata M, Atzil-Slonim D. A comparative evaluation of LLM-generated and clinician-written psychotherapy session summaries. Psychother Res 2026. doi:10.1080/10503307.2026.2729093. PMID 42715612.
sources.limitations: Summaries written by trainees, not experienced therapists. Segments, not whole sessions, with context limited to the current session. Length, terminology and structure were deliberately aligned between sources, which is why this study cannot be read as evidence that models cover more.

sources.limitations: Conversational agents rather than documentation; system-level constructs. Also a recall gap of our search: neither its title nor its abstract carries a term for notes or summarisation. Read on 2026-09-20 for the property extraction.

sources.limitations: Small panel, physicians only, emergency department; the reliability study (CJEM 2026) was not read. Read on 2026-09-20 for the property extraction.

sources.title: Myklebust KK, Bjorkly S. Development and reliability testing of the Scale for the Evaluation of Staff-Patient Interactions in Progress Notes (SESPI). Nursing Open 2019;6(3):1086-1096. doi:10.1002/nop2.254. PMID 31367401.
sources.limitations: Ten excerpts and 22 raters: the reliability claim rests on few observations, and the source itself cites Cortina on alpha being inflated for scales with many items, which is why its ICC of 0.770 is the honest figure for the instrument as a whole. Step 1 is dichotomous and the source says its ICC must be read with care. The notes are inpatient psychiatric nursing notes, not psychotherapy notes, and nothing here tests the instrument on a note written by a model. Two of its four steps score the encounter rather than the note and are recorded here as non-adoptions.

sources.title: Myklebust KK, Hoemsnes H, Kvello O, Vatnar SKB. Collaboration with clients to create journal notes: A mixed methods evaluation of a pilot intervention study in a municipality mental health services team. Counselling and Psychotherapy Research 2025;25:e12829. doi:10.1002/capr.12829.
sources.limitations: A pilot with 11 clients and 8 therapists, selection bias because most clients were never invited, no independent double scoring, and no clear date on which each client learned of the invitation, so T1 notes include notes written before the client knew. The design cannot support a causal claim and the authors do not make one. The base rates are one Norwegian municipal service, and the notes are human-written.

sources.title: Lyons D, Amos M, Mathew VM. Structured psychiatric assessment schedules - treating the case notes and the patient. Psychiatric Bulletin 2001;25:418-420. doi:10.1192/pb.25.11.418.
sources.limitations: No rater blinding, two raters, one trust, and no measure of agreement between the raters is reported, so the divergence between them is a difference in scores rather than a measured disagreement. Completion rates of the form's other categories were not studied.

sources.title: Treloar A. Improving methods of assessment in a community mental health team. Psychiatric Bulletin 1996;20:30-32. doi:10.1192/pb.20.1.30.
sources.limitations: One rater, one team, 60 notes, no blinding, and a before-and-after design in which the new form is confounded with the attention the project brought. The text layer of the published PDF interleaves two columns in the Methods section, and the quotes here are taken from a raw extraction that recovers it.

sources.title: Campbell M, Chaplin R. Improving the assessment of risk of violence: a clinical audit of case note documentation. Psychiatric Bulletin 2001;25:250-252. doi:10.1192/pb.25.7.250.
sources.limitations: Before-and-after with no control, one team, no blinding, no rater agreement, and the items come from a guideline rather than from a validated instrument.

sources.title: Comparison of accuracy of physical examination findings in initial progress notes between paper charts and a newly implemented electronic health record. J Am Med Inform Assoc 2017;24(1):140-144. doi:10.1093/jamia/ocw067. PMC7654088.
sources.limitations: Retrospective, one hospital, a transition period that confounds the medium with unfamiliarity, and general medicine rather than mental health. The reference standard works only because the chosen diagnoses have invariable findings, which is not available for a psychotherapy session.

sources.limitations: Small samples (12 to 16 respondents on the privacy items), one country, self-report, and the paper's purpose is to motivate a proposed technical solution, which is not evidence about note quality.

sources.limitations: One service, no control, the coders were not independent of the intervention, and the effect on everyday practice is indicated rather than measured. The body is German, quoted here from the English abstract.

sources.limitations: Eight providers in one setting and one country, self-report, no note was examined. The purposes they name are those of a school service billing a payer.

constructs.name: Support of claims in the source
constructs.definition: Every factual claim in the note has support in the session transcript or in another declared source. Lack of support divides into invented (the source has nothing of the kind) and distorted (the source says something else).

examples.positive: Transcript: the client says they sleep about four hours. Note: The client reports sleeping about four hours.
examples.negative: Note: The client reports insomnia since the divorce. No divorce was mentioned in the session.
examples.boundary: Note: The client seemed tired. The transcript only contains a yawn; a therapist's observation can be neither verified nor refuted from a text transcript.

constructs.applicability: Always. Unavailable context or a failed retrieval makes a claim unassessable; that is not the same as false.
constructs.error_consequences: An invented fact propagates into further care and the client reads it as something said about them.

constructs.name: Preservation of the originator of a statement
constructs.definition: The note preserves who said or observed what: the client's statement, the therapist's observation, a third party's information, information from earlier documentation.

examples.positive: The client reports that his partner reproaches him for drinking.
examples.negative: The partner reproaches the client for drinking. The client's belief has become a fact about a third person.
examples.boundary: The client agreed to try... An agreement has two originators; attributing it to one is misleading.

constructs.applicability: Requires a transcript with speaker roles. Without diarisation it cannot be measured.
constructs.error_consequences: A belief recorded as a fact about a third person is both a fidelity error and an intrusion on the rights of someone who is not the client and has no access to the note.

constructs.name: Time and change of state
constructs.definition: The note preserves when what happened and what is current as opposed to past: current state, history, intention, plan.

examples.positive: In the last session he refused; today he is considering it.
examples.negative: The client takes antidepressants. The session was about use two years ago.
examples.boundary: Plans to contact his brother. An intention voiced in the session, not an event that took place.

constructs.applicability: Longitudinal tasks require previous notes; those must not be slipped to a task that is not supposed to have them.
constructs.error_consequences: A past state presented as current changes the clinical decision.

constructs.name: Certainty, hypothesis and agreement
constructs.definition: The note preserves epistemic status: what is certain, what is the therapist's hypothesis, what is a suggestion and what is an agreement between therapist and client.

examples.positive: I am considering whether this is avoidant behaviour; to be checked in the next session.
examples.negative: This is avoidant behaviour. A consideration has become a conclusion.
examples.boundary: We agreed on a sleep diary. If the suggestion was made and the client stayed silent, it is not an agreement.

constructs.applicability: Always.
constructs.error_consequences: A suggestion elevated to an agreement creates in further care a commitment the client never signed up to.

constructs.name: Coverage of essential content weighted by importance
constructs.definition: The share of essential information from the session that the note carries, where essentiality is graded and derived from the source and the purpose, not from the existence of a field in a form.
constructs.unit: information unit derived from the source, with an assigned importance level
required_inputs: an information bank built before seeing the note

examples.positive: Self-harm was mentioned and the note carries it; an item of the Mandatory level.
examples.negative: Self-harm was mentioned and the note lacks it. One Mandatory omission weighs more than three Good-to-have omissions.
examples.boundary: The session contains nothing about medication. The item is not applicable, not unmet, and does not belong in the denominator.

candidate_formats: yes/no per unit, then a share per importance level
constructs.applicability: Information that was not said in the session must not be counted as omitted. The bank must exist before exposure to the candidate note.
constructs.error_consequences: Omitting risk information is a different class of error from omitting a homework task; blending them into one percentage erases the difference.

constructs.name: Acknowledged information gap
constructs.definition: The note distinguishes three things: that something was not said, that it was said to be absent, and that nobody asked about it.

examples.positive: Asked about suicidal thoughts, denies.
examples.negative: Suicidal thoughts: none. Nobody asked about them in the session.
examples.boundary: No risks. A summary that cannot be assigned to any question from the session.

constructs.applicability: Always, but the meaning differs by topic: an unmentioned risk is not an excluded risk.
constructs.error_consequences: A note that manufactures a negative finding gives further care false reassurance.

constructs.name: Relevance for a specific recipient
constructs.definition: What is essential changes with who reads the note and why. The same information can be necessary for taking over care and superfluous in a client summary.

examples.positive: A detail about medication is essential for continuity and optional in a client summary.
examples.negative: One relevance score across all four purposes.
examples.boundary: Risk information: the one topic where essentiality does not diverge across purposes.

constructs.applicability: Requires a purpose declared in advance. Otherwise relevance is unmeasurable.
constructs.error_consequences: A universal score rewards a note that is good for one recipient and unusable for another.

constructs.name: Risk and safety
constructs.definition: A content topic: suicidality, self-harm, danger to others, abuse, crisis markers. It is not a quality construct; it is the topic with the highest error severity. It is also a cross-cutting consequence: an error of fidelity or coverage that touches risk is more severe than the same error elsewhere.

examples.positive: A mention of hopelessness is marked as risk-related in the bank and the note carries it.
examples.negative: The mention of hopelessness is missing, and yet overall coverage comes out at 85%.
examples.boundary: The client speaks about the end ambiguously. The item is disputed, not automatically risk-related.

constructs.applicability: The topic occurs rarely; rarity is not a reason to drop the item.
constructs.error_consequences: The highest. A single omission can be clinically decisive.

constructs.name: Justification of created relations
constructs.definition: If the note connects pieces of information into a relation, a link or a conclusion, that relation is grounded in the source and appropriate to the purpose.

examples.positive: The client himself links avoiding meetings to a fear of being judged by others.
examples.negative: The note concludes social phobia although no such link was made in the session.
examples.boundary: The note calls the conversation cognitive restructuring when the therapist was only exploring how the client thinks.

candidate_formats: yes/no for support plus ordinal appropriateness
constructs.applicability: The purpose decides how much synthesis is wanted. The mere amount of clinical reasoning cannot be rewarded.
constructs.error_consequences: An invented clinical link looks like an expert conclusion and travels on.

constructs.name: Follow-through and next steps
constructs.definition: The note carries what is needed to continue: the plan, agreed tasks, open questions, the date.
constructs.unit: information unit of the plan type

examples.positive: A sleep diary agreed until the next session in a week.
examples.negative: The note states a date that was not mentioned in the session.
examples.boundary: The therapist hinted at a plan but did not agree it. A note that presents it as agreed errs in modality, not in content.

constructs.applicability: A session without an agreed plan must not be penalised for a missing plan.
constructs.error_consequences: A missing plan breaks continuity; an invented plan creates a false commitment.

constructs.name: Economy: every sentence serves something
constructs.definition: The share of sentences that carry essential content. Measured by the relation of a sentence to content, not by the length of the text. A repeated sentence still carries content, so repetition is not seen here; it is K31.

examples.positive: Four of five sentences carry essential content.
examples.negative: A one-sentence note has economy 1.00 and coverage 0.08; only both may be reported.
examples.boundary: A sentence that carries no content but holds the text together; dropping it is a debatable decision, not an error.

candidate_formats: yes/no per sentence, then a share
constructs.applicability: An empty or very short note must not receive high economy without its coverage being reported at the same time.
constructs.error_consequences: Economy reported on its own rewards an empty note.

constructs.name: Organisation and orientation in the text
constructs.definition: The note is structured so that the reader finds what they look for, and content is in its expected place.
constructs.unit: information unit times section; the whole note for overall organisation

examples.positive: The therapist's observation is in the Objective section.
examples.negative: The therapist's interpretation appears in the Subjective section as a client statement.
examples.boundary: A client quotation inside Assessment: the content belongs elsewhere, but it serves to document the conclusion.

candidate_formats: yes/no per unit times section, then a share
constructs.applicability: Only for tasks that prescribe a structure.
constructs.error_consequences: Correct content in the wrong place changes its originator and the reader reads it differently.

constructs.name: Comprehensibility for the given reader
constructs.definition: The note is linguistically comprehensible to the person it is meant for. For a client that means a different language than for a colleague.

examples.positive: The client version uses no unexplained technical terms.
examples.negative: The client version contains abbreviations without explanation.
examples.boundary: A technical term the client used in the session themselves.

constructs.applicability: Measurable only against a specific recipient.
constructs.error_consequences: An incomprehensible client summary fails its only purpose.

constructs.name: Non-stigmatising language
constructs.definition: The note does not use language that belittles the client, questions their credibility or reduces them to a diagnosis or a behaviour.

examples.positive: The client did not come to three sessions in recent weeks.
examples.negative: The client is uncooperative and manipulative.
examples.boundary: The client says of himself that he is lazy; a verbatim quotation is not the same as the author's judgement.

candidate_formats: marking of a span plus type (quotation / author)
constructs.applicability: A quotation of the client's own words is judged differently from the note author's wording.
constructs.error_consequences: The client reads a condemnation of themselves. It damages the therapeutic relationship and it is a permanent record.

constructs.name: Necessity of sensitive detail
constructs.definition: The note contains only the sensitive detail its declared purpose needs; the rest is generalised or left out.

examples.positive: The client summary mentions a family conflict without identifying the third person by name.
examples.negative: The note for supervision gives the full name and employer of the client's partner.
examples.boundary: A detail about a third person that is necessary for assessing risk.

constructs.applicability: Must not delete clinically decisive content. A conflict with a legal requirement is resolved in favour of the law and recorded.
constructs.error_consequences: Superfluous sensitive detail harms the client and third persons and cannot be taken back.

constructs.name: Context of the record's creation
constructs.definition: The note carries information about the circumstances in which it was created, because those affect how its content is to be read.

examples.positive: The note states who produced it and from what material.
examples.negative: A note created by a model presents itself as the therapist's own record.
examples.boundary: A note produced from an automatically generated transcript whose quality is not documented.

constructs.applicability: Always, but the specific mandatory fields follow from the jurisdiction.
constructs.error_consequences: Without the context of creation one cannot judge what weight to give the record.

constructs.name: Information about third persons
constructs.definition: Data about people who are not the client and gave no consent: partners, children, colleagues, other clients in a group.

examples.positive: The client describes a conflict with his superior; the note gives the role, not the name.
examples.negative: The note adopts the client's judgement of his partner as a factual description of her person.
examples.boundary: The third person is at the same time a client of the same practice.

candidate_formats: marking of a mention plus role / identification
constructs.applicability: Present in every setting. In individual therapy third parties enter through the client's account; in couple and group therapy they are participants with their own consent status, which changes the rule, not the relevance.
constructs.error_consequences: Intrudes on the rights of someone who does not know about the note and has no access to it.

constructs.name: Traceability of claims to the source
constructs.definition: For a claim, the place in the source that supports it can be shown. Distinguished are the validity of the citation, its actual support of the claim, and the share of claims that carry a citation. The object is the citation the author writes into the note; the evidence spans an evaluator attaches while checking a claim are a different thing and belong to the methods.
constructs.unit: a citation and the claim it cites for

examples.positive: A claim cites a turn in the transcript that actually contains it.
examples.negative: A citation points to an existing turn that says nothing about the claim.
examples.boundary: A citation points to a turn that supports the claim only together with another turn.

constructs.applicability: Only for tasks that explicitly require citations. An ordinary time in square brackets is not a citation.
constructs.error_consequences: A citation that does not support inspires false confidence more effectively than no citation.

constructs.name: Required elements of Czech medical documentation, where it applies
constructs.definition: The note carries the elements the current Czech regulation requires of medical documentation. The decree is a requirements source and the observable criterion is the presence of those elements. It binds a narrow population: records kept by a provider of health services, in practice clinical psychologists. A therapist working outside health services keeps no medical documentation and this criterion does not reach them.

examples.positive: The note carries the identification of the author of the entry.
examples.negative: The note has no author field because a model produced it.
examples.boundary: A note meant for the client is not medical documentation and these criteria do not apply to it.

constructs.applicability: Czech notes only, and only those kept as medical documentation by a provider of health services. Not the English track, not a client summary, which is not medical documentation at all. The decree prescribes required elements, not a note structure: no SOAP, DAP or BIRP form is mandatory in the Czech Republic, so the criterion must never be read as a requirement to write in one of them.
constructs.error_consequences: A missing required element is a documentation problem for the narrow population this binds, not a clinical defect of the note, and it must not be mixed into a quality score. Reading it as a legal verdict would be a claim about real practice that this work cannot support.

constructs.name: Compliance with the task's format
constructs.definition: The note kept to what the instruction explicitly asked for: sections, length, language, forbidden elements.

examples.positive: The note has all four required headings.
examples.negative: The note exceeded the word limit.
examples.boundary: The note kept within the limit by leaving out risk information.

constructs.applicability: Only where the task explicitly asks for the check.
constructs.error_consequences: Small, unless mistaken for quality.

constructs.name: Taking over care from the note
constructs.definition: Another professional can meaningfully continue care from the note without access to the transcript.

examples.positive: After reading, the therapist knows what was agreed and what to build on.
examples.negative: The therapist has to reach for the transcript to understand at all what it was about.
examples.boundary: The note suffices for continuity but not for assessing risk.

constructs.applicability: Requires a person in the role of the one taking over. An LLM cannot stand in for this task.
constructs.error_consequences: This is the quantity notes are written for; not tracking it is the main weakness of purely textual measures.

constructs.name: Extent and nature of the edits needed
constructs.definition: How many and what kinds of intervention a professional has to make before the note is usable. The type of edit carries information that a score does not.

examples.positive: The therapist corrects one formulation.
examples.negative: The therapist rewrites three of four sections.
examples.boundary: The therapist changes nothing because there is no time to check. Zero edits then do not mean quality.

constructs.applicability: Requires a real workflow, not laboratory rating.
constructs.error_consequences: Low visible error rate with a high rate of silent rewriting hides the real state.

constructs.name: Acceptability: would a professional use this in practice
constructs.definition: Whether a professional would take the note into their own practice and keep using the system that produced it, and if not, why. The question is about use, not about billing or any payer. It is answered on the six parameters MentalCLOUDS took from the acceptability framework for health-care interventions: affective attitude, burden, ethicality, coherence, opportunity costs and perceived effectiveness. Only coherence is a property of the text; the other five are about what working with it costs.

examples.positive: The therapist would keep using the system and would file this note as it is.
examples.negative: The therapist will not use it, although the note is factually correct, because checking it costs more than writing the note themselves.
examples.boundary: The note is acceptable and the therapist would still not use the system, for a reason that is not about this note at all.

constructs.applicability: A human measurement. Cannot be replaced by a judge.
constructs.error_consequences: A benchmark that measures only text can recommend a system that professionals reject.

constructs.name: Understanding and acceptance by the client
constructs.definition: Whether the client understands the summary, recognises their session in it, and is not harmed by reading it.

examples.positive: The client reads the summary and confirms that it matches what they experienced.
examples.negative: The client finds in the summary a statement they do not recognise about themselves.
examples.boundary: The summary is factually correct and the client perceives it as cold.

constructs.applicability: Requires real readers. Does not fit into the first pilot without an ethics framework.
constructs.error_consequences: The most sensitive purpose; an error touches the client directly.

constructs.name: Support of the supervision task
constructs.definition: Whether a supervisor can tell from the note what the therapist did, why, and where they were unsure.

examples.positive: The supervisor recognises the chosen intervention and the client's reaction to it.
examples.negative: The note describes the content of the session but not what the therapist did.
examples.boundary: The note is sufficient for continuity and empty for supervision.

constructs.applicability: Requires supervisors as raters.
constructs.error_consequences: Supervision without information about the therapist's procedure misses its point.

constructs.name: Consistency across sessions
constructs.definition: The note does not contradict earlier notes of the same case where there is no documented reason for it.
constructs.unit: pair of notes of the same case

examples.positive: The note records a change of state and refers to the earlier one.
examples.negative: The note records the first mention of panic attacks although the previous note contains them.
examples.boundary: The contradiction corresponds to a real change in what the client said between sessions.

constructs.applicability: Requires a series of notes of the same case with a validated chronology. The current cases are not prepared or selected for longitudinal evaluation: the native sessions carry no validated session order and stay outside the pilot by decision D1, so the candidate is not measured in this round.
constructs.error_consequences: A contradiction in the documentation undermines the credibility of the whole record.

constructs.name: Evenness of quality across client groups
constructs.definition: Whether note quality does not systematically drop for certain client groups, language varieties or topics.
constructs.unit: group of cases, not an individual note

examples.positive: Risk coverage is comparable across subgroups.
examples.negative: The model reliably omits content for clients speaking non-standard language.
examples.boundary: A difference exists but corresponds to a real difference in the content of the sessions.

candidate_formats: breakdown of existing scores by subgroup
constructs.applicability: Requires enough cases per subgroup. With one Czech client cluster it CANNOT be measured and must not be pretended to be.
constructs.error_consequences: Systematic inequality is worse than random error and a single note does not reveal it.

constructs.name: Personalisation: a note about this person
constructs.definition: The note captures what is unique about this client and this session, instead of a generic description that would fit anyone. Not a matter of style but of whether the text carries idiosyncratic content.
constructs.unit: the set of notes of one system, not one note
required_inputs: notes from the same generator across several cases

examples.positive: The note records that the client speaks about his father exclusively in work metaphors.
examples.negative: The note records that the client showed anxiety and was motivated to change. It fits any session and is at the same time fully faithful and complete.
examples.boundary: The session itself was poor in content; a generic note may then be adequate.

candidate_formats: continuous score from embeddings and self-ROUGE
constructs.applicability: CANNOT be measured on one note. Requires enough cases to compute similarity among them.
constructs.error_consequences: A generic note passes every other criterion and adds nothing that would help the next therapist recognise this client.

constructs.name: Information density
constructs.definition: How much clinically essential content the note carries per unit of text. Not length and not economy: the ratio between information carried and space consumed.
constructs.unit: note; comparable only among notes of the same source material

examples.positive: Two notes of the same length; one carries nine essential pieces of information, the other four.
examples.negative: A model has higher coverage simply because it wrote twice as much text. We report it as better coverage although per page it carries less.
examples.boundary: A longer note that additionally carries only marginal information: higher coverage, lower density, and worse for the reader.

candidate_formats: continuous ratio (distinct units per language-specific length unit)
constructs.applicability: Without comparable length or without normalisation per unit of text, coverage comparisons between systems are misleading. A short note can be dense and still omit essential content; density is never read alone.
constructs.error_consequences: Without it the benchmark systematically rewards verbosity. That is precisely the tendency models have, so the error always points one way.

constructs.name: Language naturalness
constructs.definition: The note reads as a clinician of that language would write it: ordinary clinical register, no machine phrasing, no idiom carried over from another language. Distinct from comprehensibility: a stilted note can be perfectly understandable.

examples.positive: The note reads as a clinician wrote it, in the ordinary register of the language.
examples.negative: The note repeats one template phrase in every section and renders English idioms word for word in Czech.
examples.boundary: A note that is grammatical and comprehensible but stilted: comprehensibility (K13) passes and naturalness is the open question.

candidate_formats: ordinal scale per note; not yet defined
constructs.applicability: Both languages, each with its own operationalisation: what reads as natural in Czech clinical writing is not a translation of the English rule. Requires human raters; no automatic proxy is proposed.
constructs.error_consequences: Low for care; an unnatural note is still read. It marks the text as machine-written and can lower trust in the content.

constructs.name: Redundancy: the same fact more than once
constructs.definition: An essential information unit appears in the note more than once without new content. Not economy: a repeated sentence still carries content, so the share of content-bearing sentences (K11) does not see it. Not density: density also falls with padding that repeats nothing.
constructs.unit: information unit repeated within one note

examples.positive: Each essential unit appears once, in its section.
examples.negative: The client's panic attacks are described in Subjective, again in Assessment and again in Plan, with nothing new each time.
examples.boundary: A fact restated in Plan with a new next step attached is not repetition.

candidate_formats: count of repeated units per note, then a share; not yet defined
constructs.applicability: Any note; needs the same unit bank as coverage. A restatement that adds a consequence, such as a next step, is not repetition.
constructs.error_consequences: Moderate: repetition lengthens the note, hides omissions behind volume and inflates any comparison that grows with length.

constructs.name: Cultural competence evidenced in the note
constructs.definition: The note shows that the client's cultural, linguistic and social context was taken into account where it bore on the session: how the client's background is recorded, whether an adaptation or an interpreter is noted, and that no assumption about the client stands in for what was said. It is judged from the note alone, as what the note shows about the care.

examples.positive: The note records that the client's religious framing of guilt was taken up in the intervention in the client's own terms.
examples.negative: The note explains the client's reluctance by a cultural stereotype the session does not contain.
examples.boundary: The transcript carries no cultural content; the note says nothing about it and the item is not applicable.

candidate_formats: human judgement; scale not yet defined
constructs.applicability: Where the session carries cultural, linguistic or social context that bore on the care. A session without such content makes the item not applicable, which is not a failure.
constructs.error_consequences: A note that reads the client through a stereotype is read by the next clinician and by the client; the harm is to the relationship and to trust, and it is permanent.

constructs.name: Internal consistency within one note
constructs.definition: No part of the note ignores or contradicts another part of the same note. Distinct from K26, which is consistency between notes of one case, and from K01: two statements can each have support in the source at different moments and still contradict each other when the note presents both as current.
constructs.unit: pair of statements within one note

examples.positive: The plan in the Plan section follows from the assessment above it.
examples.negative: The Subjective section says the client stopped drinking; the Plan section plans to reduce the drinking.
examples.boundary: The note reports that the client said two contradictory things in the session; that is faithful reporting, not an inconsistency of the note.

candidate_formats: categorical per pair of contradicting statements; not yet defined
constructs.applicability: Any note. A contradiction the client themselves voiced and the note reports as the client's is fidelity, not inconsistency.
constructs.error_consequences: A reader who finds a contradiction cannot tell which part to trust and discounts the whole note.

constructs.name: Correct and appropriate professional terminology
constructs.definition: The note names what happened in the words the profession uses, and uses them correctly: a term stands for what the term means, a lay paraphrase does not replace a term that carries clinical meaning, and no term is used that the session does not support. Distinct from K30, which is whether the text reads as a clinician of that language would write it: a fluent note can use the wrong term, and a correct term can sit in a stilted sentence. Distinct from K13, which is whether the intended reader understands it.

examples.positive: The note writes that the client reports early waking and loss of interest, and calls the latter anhedonia where the session's content supports it.
examples.negative: The note calls the client's described worry a panic attack, which the session does not describe.
examples.boundary: The note writes „the client was somehow out of it“: not a wrong term, a missing one, which is the same failure from the other side.

candidate_formats: ordinal per note, or categorical per term; not yet defined
constructs.applicability: Both languages, each with its own rule: Czech clinical terminology is not a translation of the English list, and for the client purpose the requirement inverts, because a note a client reads should not lean on terms.
constructs.error_consequences: A wrong term is read by the next clinician as a finding, and a term the session does not support is a diagnosis nobody made. A missing term costs precision rather than safety.

constructs.name: The interaction is described from both sides
constructs.definition: The note describes what the therapist did and how the client responded to it, not one without the other. The source's instrument orders this in four levels: the therapist's approach is missing or too thin to read; the approach is there but not the client's response; the approach is there and met practically, without reaching the client's experience or feelings; both the approach and the client's response are there. Distinct from K25, which asks whether a supervisor can tell what the therapist did and why: a note can answer that and still say nothing about what it did to the client. Distinct from K02, which is attribution, who said a thing: this is whether the exchange is there at all.
constructs.unit: the note, or an excerpt of it; the instrument was tested on excerpts and the 2025 application scored whole journal notes, so which unit a level belongs to is not settled by the source and has to be declared

examples.positive: The note records that the therapist named the client's silence and asked what it was protecting, and that the client said it felt safer not to answer yet.
examples.negative: The note records that the therapist worked on the client's avoidance, and says nothing about how the client took it.
examples.boundary: The note records that the client asked for a letter for their employer and that the therapist agreed to write one. The approach is practical and the client accepted it, and the client's experience of the session is absent: the source's level C rather than D.

candidate_formats: ordinal, four levels, from the source's manual
constructs.applicability: Both languages. The rule reads the note alone, so it needs no transcript, which also means it cannot tell a described interaction from an invented one: a model that writes a plausible exchange that did not happen scores D here and fails K01.
constructs.error_consequences: Scored from the note alone, a confident invention of an exchange is indistinguishable from an accurate record of one. The level must never be read as evidence that the interaction happened, and must be reported beside K01.

constructs.name: The client's experience is in the note, not only their behaviour
constructs.definition: The note carries some description of how the client experienced something, and not only what the client was observed to do. The source's instrument asks this as a yes-or-no gate before anything else is scored, and its own example of a no is a note that reports only conduct. Distinct from K05, which asks whether the substantive content of the session is there: a note can cover the session's topics completely and report none of the client's experience of them. Distinct from K28, which asks whether what is there is specific to this client rather than generic.
constructs.unit: the note, or an excerpt of it; the same unresolved unit as K35

examples.positive: The note records that the client said the week felt like wading, and that getting up was the hardest part of the day.
examples.negative: The note records that the client attended, spoke little and left on time.
examples.boundary: The note records a diagnosis-shaped summary, that the client presented with low mood and reduced motivation, and nothing of how the client described it. Whether clinical wording of a state counts as the client's experience is the judgement the rule has to settle, and the source settles it by asking for the client's own experience.

candidate_formats: dichotomous in the source; an ordinal form is possible and is not the source's
constructs.applicability: Both languages. Read from the note alone, so as with K35 it cannot distinguish a described experience from an invented one.
constructs.error_consequences: Used as a gate, as the source uses it, it removes the worst notes from every other measure. Reported as a property, its cost is only that a note of pure conduct is marked as such.

measurements.definition: Each information unit the note carries is checked against the section the task's template expects it in.
measurements.question: Is every information unit the note carries placed in the section the template expects for it?

anchors.pass: every unit the note carries sits in its expected section
anchors.fail: at least one unit sits in another section; each such unit is marked

examples.pass: The client's report of drinking is in Subjective and the plan to cut down is in Plan.
examples.fail: The therapist's working hypothesis about avoidance is written into Subjective as the client's statement.

cs.definition: Každá informační jednotka, kterou zápis nese, se porovná s oddílem, kde ji šablona úlohy čeká.
cs.question: Stojí každá informační jednotka, kterou zápis nese, v oddílu, kde ji šablona čeká?

anchors.pass: každá jednotka, kterou zápis nese, stojí ve svém očekávaném oddílu
anchors.fail: aspoň jedna jednotka stojí v jiném oddílu; každá taková se označí

examples.pass: Klientova zpráva o pití je v části Subjektivní a plán omezit pití v části Plán.
examples.fail: Pracovní hypotéza terapeuta o vyhýbání je zapsaná v části Subjektivní jako výrok klienta.

measurements.definition: Each sentence of the note is labelled with the information units it carries; a sentence that carries none is superfluous. The share is reported beside coverage.
measurements.question: Does every sentence of the note carry at least one information unit of the bank?

anchors.pass: every sentence carries at least one unit, or is a required heading
anchors.fail: at least one sentence carries no unit; each such sentence is marked

examples.pass: Every sentence names something the client said, the therapist did, or the plan holds.
examples.fail: "The session was productive and the client engaged well" carries no unit of the bank.

cs.definition: Každá věta zápisu se označí informačními jednotkami, které nese; věta, která nenese žádnou, je nadbytečná. Podíl se uvádí vedle pokrytí.
cs.question: Nese každá věta zápisu aspoň jednu informační jednotku banky?

anchors.pass: každá věta nese aspoň jednu jednotku, nebo je to povinný nadpis
anchors.fail: aspoň jedna věta nenese žádnou jednotku; každá taková se označí

examples.pass: Každá věta pojmenovává něco, co klient řekl, terapeut udělal nebo plán obsahuje.
examples.fail: „Sezení bylo produktivní a klient dobře spolupracoval“ nenese žádnou jednotku banky.

measurements.definition: The author's own text of the note is read for wording that stigmatises the client or another person; a quotation of the client's words is marked as quotation and is not the author's text. No word list decides this; a rater does, and marks the span.
measurements.question: Is the author's own text of the note free of wording that stigmatises the client or another person?

anchors.pass: no span of the author's text stigmatises anyone
anchors.fail: at least one span of the author's text stigmatises the client or another person; each span is marked with its type

examples.pass: The note writes that the client reports drinking daily and describes his wife as angry about it.
examples.fail: The note calls the client an alcoholic who manipulates his wife; the transcript carries neither word.

cs.definition: Vlastní text autora zápisu se čte kvůli formulacím, které stigmatizují klienta nebo jinou osobu; citace klientových slov se označí jako citace a není textem autora. Nerozhoduje seznam slov, rozhoduje hodnotitel a označí úsek.
cs.question: Je vlastní text autora zápisu prostý formulací, které stigmatizují klienta nebo jinou osobu?

anchors.pass: žádný úsek textu autora nikoho nestigmatizuje
anchors.fail: aspoň jeden úsek textu autora stigmatizuje klienta nebo jinou osobu; každý úsek se označí s typem

examples.pass: Zápis píše, že klient uvádí každodenní pití a popisuje, že se na něj žena kvůli tomu zlobí.
examples.fail: Zápis nazývá klienta alkoholikem, který manipuluje svou ženou; přepis nenese ani jedno z těch slov.

method_specs.definition: Before any note is read, a bank of information units is built from the transcript. Each unit is one fact that a continuation of care or a documentation audit would need, and carries an importance level (mandatory, mandatory in certain circumstances, highly recommended, good to have, optional), a purpose tag (continuity, audit), a type tag (plan, risk, other) and the transcript span it rests on. For each unit the answerer receives the note only and states whether the note carries it. The answer is compared with the bank. Coverage is reported per importance level and per purpose, never as one sum (P01); a unit the note reports as not asked or as explicitly denied is answered with that status, not as omitted (P02); risk-tagged units are reported as their own layer that no other unit can dilute (P03).
method_specs.applicability: Any note written from a transcript that a bank was built from. A unit the transcript does not contain cannot be in the bank. A bank is built and approved before the notes are seen; a unit added after a note was read is recorded as such and excluded.

outcomes.preserved: the note carries the unit with the same content, actor and time
outcomes.partial: the note carries part of the unit, or with an unclear referent or time
outcomes.omitted: the note does not carry the unit and does not say that it is missing
outcomes.contradicted: the note states the opposite of the unit, reports as not asked what the transcript asked, or reports as denied what the transcript affirmed
outcomes.unassessable: the answerer cannot decide from the note; recorded as such, never as omitted

severity_rules.none: preserved, or the omission of an optional unit
severity_rules.minor: partial, or the omission of a good-to-have unit
severity_rules.major: the omission of a highly recommended or mandatory unit, or the contradiction of a unit that is not risk-tagged
severity_rules.critical: any contradiction or omission of a risk-tagged unit, or a fabricated gap: the note reports as not asked or as denied what the transcript carries

cs.definition: Dříve, než kdokoli čte zápis, se z přepisu sestaví banka informačních jednotek. Každá jednotka je jeden fakt, který by potřebovalo navázání péče nebo kontrola dokumentace, a nese stupeň důležitosti (povinné, povinné za určitých okolností, silně doporučené, dobré mít, volitelné), značku účelu (návaznost, kontrola), značku typu (plán, riziko, ostatní) a úsek přepisu, o který se opírá. U každé jednotky dostane odpovídající pouze zápis a řekne, zda ho zápis nese. Odpověď se porovná s bankou. Pokrytí se uvádí po stupních důležitosti a po účelech, nikdy jako jeden součet (P01); jednotku, o které zápis říká, že nebyla probrána nebo že ji klient výslovně popřel, se hodnotí tímto statusem, ne jako vynechanou (P02); jednotky označené jako riziko se uvádějí jako vlastní vrstva, kterou žádná jiná jednotka nerozředí (P03).

outcomes.preserved: zápis jednotku nese se stejným obsahem, aktérem i časem
outcomes.partial: zápis nese část jednotky, nebo s nejasným vztažením či časem
outcomes.omitted: zápis jednotku nenese a neříká, že chybí
outcomes.contradicted: zápis tvrdí opak jednotky, uvádí jako neprobrané to, na co se v přepisu ptalo, nebo jako popřené to, co přepis potvrzuje
outcomes.unassessable: odpovídající to ze zápisu nedokáže rozhodnout; zapíše se tak, nikdy jako vynechané

severity_rules.minor: částečně, nebo vynechání jednotky typu dobré mít
severity_rules.major: vynechání silně doporučené nebo povinné jednotky, nebo popření jednotky, která není označená jako riziko
severity_rules.critical: jakékoli popření nebo vynechání jednotky označené jako riziko, nebo vymyšlená mezera: zápis uvádí jako neprobrané nebo popřené to, co přepis nese

cs.applicability: Jakýkoli zápis psaný z přepisu, ze kterého byla sestavena banka. Jednotka, kterou přepis neobsahuje, v bance být nemůže. Banka se sestaví a schválí dříve, než se čtou zápisy; jednotka přidaná po přečtení zápisu se tak zaznamená a vyloučí.

method_specs.definition: The note is decomposed into atomic claims. Each claim carries its actor (who said or did it), its time (when, and whether it is a change of state) and its modality (fact, hypothesis, plan, agreement, degree of certainty). Each claim is verified against the transcript (P04). A claim that has support in the transcript at a different actor, time or modality is contradicted, and the error is typed as actor, time or modality (P05).
method_specs.applicability: Every declarative sentence of the note. Section headings and template text are not claims. A statement the note attributes to the client as reported speech is verified as what the client said, not as a fact about the client.

outcomes.supported: the transcript carries the claim with the same actor, time and modality
outcomes.contradicted: the transcript carries the opposite, or the same content at a different actor, time or modality; the error type is recorded
outcomes.unsupported: the transcript carries nothing that supports or contradicts the claim
outcomes.unassessable: the claim cannot be decided from the transcript; recorded as such

severity_rules.minor: an unsupported detail without clinical consequence, or an unassessable claim
severity_rules.major: an unsupported claim about the client's state, history or plan, or an actor, time or modality error that changes who, when or how certain
severity_rules.critical: a contradicted claim about risk, safety, diagnosis, medication or a decision of care, or an intervention attributed to the therapist that the transcript does not carry

cs.definition: Zápis se rozloží na atomická tvrzení. Každé tvrzení nese svého aktéra (kdo to řekl nebo udělal), čas (kdy, a zda jde o změnu stavu) a modalitu (fakt, hypotéza, plán, dohoda, míra jistoty). Každé tvrzení se ověří proti přepisu (P04). Tvrzení, které má v přepisu oporu u jiného aktéra, v jiném čase nebo v jiné modalitě, je popřené a chyba se zařadí jako chyba aktéra, času nebo modality (P05).

outcomes.supported: přepis nese tvrzení se stejným aktérem, časem i modalitou
outcomes.contradicted: přepis nese opak, nebo stejný obsah u jiného aktéra, v jiném čase nebo v jiné modalitě; typ chyby se zapíše
outcomes.unsupported: přepis nenese nic, co by tvrzení podpíralo nebo popíralo
outcomes.unassessable: tvrzení nelze z přepisu rozhodnout; zapíše se tak

severity_rules.minor: nepodložený detail bez klinického důsledku, nebo nerozhodnutelné tvrzení
severity_rules.major: nepodložené tvrzení o stavu, historii nebo plánu klienta, nebo chyba aktéra, času či modality, která mění kdo, kdy nebo s jakou jistotou
severity_rules.critical: popřené tvrzení o riziku, bezpečí, diagnóze, medikaci nebo rozhodnutí o péči, nebo intervence připsaná terapeutovi, kterou přepis nenese

cs.applicability: Každá oznamovací věta zápisu. Nadpisy oddílů a text šablony nejsou tvrzení. Výrok, který zápis připisuje klientovi jako řeč klienta, se ověřuje jako to, co klient řekl, ne jako fakt o klientovi.

method_specs.definition: Rubric items rated per note by a rater who has the transcript, the note and the section template: whether content sits in the section the template expects (P06), whether every sentence carries an information unit (P07), and whether the author's own text, as distinct from quotation of the client, contains stigmatising wording (P08). P07 is reported beside coverage and never alone, because an empty note passes it.
method_specs.unit: item per note; P06 per unit and section, P07 per sentence, P08 per span of text
method_specs.applicability: P06 only where the task prescribes sections; P07 and P08 for every note. A quotation of the client's own words is not the author's text for P08.

outcomes.pass: the item's condition holds for the whole note
outcomes.fail: the item's condition fails at least once; the place is marked
outcomes.rated: an ordinal or categorical item was rated; the label is recorded
outcomes.not_applicable: the item does not apply to this note, with the reason
outcomes.unassessable: the rater cannot decide; recorded as such, never as fail

severity_rules.minor: a unit in another section (P06), or a sentence that carries no unit (P07)
severity_rules.major: stigmatising wording in the author's own text (P08)
severity_rules.critical: stigmatising wording that attributes to the client a trait or motive the transcript does not carry

cs.definition: Rubrikové položky hodnocené na celém zápisu hodnotitelem, který má přepis, zápis a šablonu oddílů: zda obsah stojí v oddílu, kde ho šablona čeká (P06), zda každá věta nese informační jednotku (P07) a zda vlastní text autora, na rozdíl od citace klienta, obsahuje stigmatizující formulaci (P08). P07 se uvádí vedle pokrytí a nikdy samo, protože prázdný zápis jím projde.

outcomes.pass: podmínka položky platí pro celý zápis
outcomes.fail: podmínka položky aspoň jednou neplatí; místo se označí
outcomes.rated: ordinální nebo kategoriální položka byla ohodnocena; štítek se zapíše
outcomes.not_applicable: položka se na tento zápis nevztahuje, s důvodem
outcomes.unassessable: hodnotitel to nedokáže rozhodnout; zapíše se tak, nikdy jako selhání

severity_rules.minor: jednotka v jiném oddílu (P06), nebo věta, která nenese žádnou jednotku (P07)
severity_rules.major: stigmatizující formulace ve vlastním textu autora (P08)
severity_rules.critical: stigmatizující formulace, která klientovi připisuje rys nebo motiv, který přepis nenese

cs.applicability: P06 jen tam, kde úloha předepisuje oddíly; P07 a P08 u každého zápisu. Citace klientových vlastních slov není pro P08 text autora.

assessment_scope: Feasibility pilot under research protocol 2.3.0: the two public AnnoMI conversations drawn in pilot-cases.json (94 and 25) in English and their recorded Czech translations, notes written for the continuity and audit purposes by two generator families, measured by source-bank question answering (qa), atomic-claim verification (claims) and rubric items (items), with a human anchor of two Czech psychologists under the protocol's crossover; no citation method in this round.
